Accepted. Format is valid: STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES headers present, FINAL_STATES nonempty with u6 declared and accepting (exit reached with the box held), transition/reward syntax matches the paper format, and every reward entry references a declared transition.

Semantic fidelity is good. u2 and u4 act as one-step 'must re-pickup now' windows after each fall: entering u2/u4 via box_fell, the next step must show holding_box (u2/u4 -> u3) or, in the corner case where the second scheduled fall fires on that same step, box_fell again (u2 -> u4, rewarded 0.2); anything else goes to the absorbing failure state u5. This correctly encodes 'the move right after the fall has to pick it up' as a hard requirement. All exit-without-box paths (u0/u1 via at_exit & !holding_box, u2/u4 via !holding_box & !box_fell) also land in u5, encoding 'do not reach the exit without the box'. u6 pays 1.0 only from u1/u3 on at_exit & holding_box, so success requires the box in hands and every observed fall immediately recovered. The strict u5 trap (zero reward forever, so a later exit with the box earns nothing after a missed re-pickup) matches the 'has to' wording. The (u2, box_fell, u4) -> 0.2 entry is reachable, not a reward for falling: after a fall the hands are empty, so box_fell on the next step is only possible if the agent picked up (compliance) and the second fall fired on that step, mirroring the u2->u3 compliance reward.

Safety and coverage check out. Rewards are bounded (max ~1.3: 0.1 first pickup + one 0.2 + 1.0 exit), no negative rewards, and no reward-paying cycles (u3->u4->u3 pays 0; u2/u4 are exited every step; u0/u1 re-pickups fall to unrewarded else loops, so no 0.1/0.2 farming; at most two falls per episode cap the 0.2s). Guards within each state are mutually exclusive given the environment constraints (box_feld never co-occurs with holding_box or at_exit), and every state has an else self-loop, so all assignments — including the task-irrelevant siren_ringing/switch_toggled — are covered; the siren is correctly ignored throughout.

Non-blocking notes for the record: (1) (u4, holding_box & !at_exit & !box_fell, u3) has no reward while its u2 counterpart gives 0.2, so the immediate re-pickup after the second fall is enforced but never shaped — enforcement is unaffected (a miss still traps in u5 and the exit reward remains reachable only from u3), but adding 0.2 there would make progress shaping symmetric and denser. (2) Several dead transitions exist and are harmless but could be pruned: (u0, box_fell)->u2 (a fall requires a previously observed holding_box, so u0 can never see box_fell), (u0/u2/u4, at_exit & holding_box)->u6 (a pickup cannot coincide with the move onto the exit, and box_fell/at_exit never co-occur), and (u4, box_fell)->u4 (a third fall is impossible). None of these carries an exploitable reward path. (3) The persistent/event distinction is handled correctly: one-step box_fell is latched into the u2/u4 awaiting states while holding_box is used as a condition, and at_exit guards are terminal-only as the environment guarantees.

def siren_ringing(env): return env.siren_ringing

def switch_toggled(env): return "toggle" in env.events_this_step

def holding_box(env): return env.carrying is not None and env.carrying.type == "box"

def box_fell(env): return "fall" in env.events_this_step

def at_exit(env): return env.grid.get(*env.agent_pos) is not None and env.grid.get(*env.agent_pos).type == "goal"
